failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who was Princess Charlotte of Lorraine? What were the genealogical relationships and descendants of each Princess Charlotte of Lorraine's father? How do the descendants of Princess Charlotte of Lorraine's father connect to Umberto II of Italy?' Hop 3 query: 'Was Princess Charlotte of Lorraine (1678-1757) the daughter of Louis, Count of Armagnac, and does genealogical documentation confirm that Louis, Count of Armagnac's descendants include Umberto II, the last king of Italy?' Both queries target the same three facts (Charlotte's identity, her father's identity, and the genealogical link to Umberto II) that were already fully answered in hop 2. Hop 3 retrieves the same two core documents (Charlotte of Lorraine and Louis, Count of Armagnac passages) that appeared in hop 2, plus eight irrelevant historical Counts of Armagnac from different centuries.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 3, the agent was presented with 10 documents, 8 of which concerned historical Counts of Armagnac from the 14th-15th centuries (John II, Charles I, Louis d'Armagnac Duke of Nemours, Bernard VII, Joan of Armagnac, Bonne of Armagnac, John V) who have no connection to the claim about Charlotte of Lorraine (1678-1757) and Louis, Count of Armagnac (1641-1718). These passages were clearly irrelevant as they predate the relevant individuals by 200-300 years, yet the retrieval system devoted resources to fetching them after the coordinator's hop 3 query.
